prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1178; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss for a low-speed head-on collision. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed into their lane on a curve. Both vehicles driven from scene. Claimant reports neck and back strain and has retained counsel, who has requested that all contact go through the firm.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation and receive the letter of protection. Requested medical authorizations and prior treatment records for the cervical and lumbar spine. Scene photos and repair estimates for both vehicles uploaded to file. Liability appears probable for the other driver based on the lane-encroachment account and the damage pattern.

Entry 3: Reviewed the independent appraisal. Damage to the front bumper, hood, and radiator support is consistent with a low-speed frontal impact. Airbag did not deploy in either vehicle. Requested the event data recorder download for the claimant's vehicle through counsel before the vehicle is released for repair.

Entry 4: Received initial treatment records showing evaluation at an urgent care facility followed by referral to physical therapy. Diagnosis recorded as cervical and lumbar strain with muscle spasm. No imaging of the spine reported at this time. Attorney's office indicates a demand package will follow once treatment concludes.

Entry 5: Diary set for follow-up with claimant's counsel on outstanding treatment records and the event data recorder report. Reserves reviewed and held pending receipt of the demand. Supervisor notified that the claim involves represented claimant and possible bodily injury exposure.
